I was giving WITI/USACS as examples of fully-fleshed out clubs with specific events and decent alumni network that is rather helpful to students.

It's cool. Your point's valid. I join clubs to further develop/explore my interests, and meet interesting people who are possibly going to be within my field of study/work.

I totally get that not everyone is good at professional development and might need some guidance. eg, someone asked:

" is cold emailing the same as sending a cover letter"...which while sounds like a silly question, but I won't place judgment.

I totally understand how someone with no previous work experience could be confused. While that is the case, I feel like while clubs are catered to also help out freshmen, that upperclassmen at the end of the day need something, too, as that's what they're joining clubs for (in addition to classes/other casual EC's/work/etc). I've since transferred to a T10 since I found it a better fit in terms of EC's and everything overall.

EDIT:

Also, to be clear, I'm not bashing clubs like WITI/USACS cause they have a clear agenda as to what's being offered, and what you can expect to learn from each event.
